title: Anapole and electric-dipole dark matter versus the LZ event: contact and photon-mediated versions
question: Can photon-mediated anapole (O8+O9) or electric-dipole (O11/q^2) dark matter, or their heavy-mediator contact analogues, produce a lone 248 keV xenon recoil; what moments does LZ's 1.0-event fit imply; and which NR structure is LZ's 3.4-sigma L16?
headline_result: At 1 TeV the photon anapole leaves 26.9 (O8 charge scatters) and the photon EDM 18 100 events in 5.4-55 keV per 200-270 keV event; only q-weighted pure-spin structures (O9 2.07, O11xq^2 2.19, O9xq^2 0.024) are compatible, so L16 is not the anapole but a companion-free q^4-spin operator degenerate with L10 (190-490 events to separate); the fitted event implies A = 2.7e-6 GeV^-2 = (605 GeV)^-2 and d_E = 3.3e-24 e cm, with 2024-null bounds A <= 4.4e-6 GeV^-2 and d_E <= 5.6e-24 e cm
key_numbers: N_lo(1 TeV): anapole 26.9 (200/4000 GeV 82/23; O8-only 1264, O9-only 2.2, sign flip 25.2), heavy-vector A-V F2=0 946, anapole x q^2 0.29, photon EDM 18100 (54100/15600), contact O11 (proton) 118, O11 x q^2 2.19, O9 2.07, O9 x q^2 0.024, O14 2.35, L10 0.199; A(1 ROI event) 1.32e-6/2.73e-6/5.38e-6 GeV^-2 at 200/1000/4000 GeV, A(1 hi event) 1.59e-5 -> 39.8 events in 2024; A bound 4.36e-6 (tol 3); d_E(1 ROI) 1.50e-24/3.28e-24/6.54e-24 e cm, d_E(1 hi) 5.3e-22 -> 26800 companions; d_E bound 5.6e-24; Z_pred anapole 2.71, O9 3.12, O9xq2 >=3.4; peaks O9xq2 214 keV vs L10 199; N_3sigma vs L10: anapole 5, O9 46, O9xq2 190-200, anapole x q^2 370-490; c8/c9 reduction matches directdm exactly, c11 to 1%
model_or_mechanism: NREFT (Anand/Fitzpatrick) with WimPyDD: anapole c8=2eAQ_N, c9=eAg_N (contact after photon EOM); EDM c11=2e d_E Q_N m_N/q^2 (long range); contact O11, O11 x q^2, F2=0 A-V, q^2-anapole; pure O9, O9 x q^2, O14; L10 reference (P012); P016 Z(N_lo) calibration; KL separation test
confidence: medium: N_lo and couplings cross-checked against P003/P012/P031 to 1%; L16 identification rests on recalled reductions and a 1D Z(N_lo) proxy
